description: NexHunters Bionic Labs is building EARTHSCOPE, an interactive platform for climate-resilient farming. For NASA Space Apps 2026’s Field Shift challenge, we aim to combine NASA Earth observations, soil information and crop characteristics to help farmers compare crop rotations, water needs, climate risks, costs and potential yields. We welcome teammates with skills in agriculture, Earth science, satellite data.
summary:
EARTHSCOPE GodView turns any point on Earth into a live evidence board — weather, hazards, soil, crops, prices and news, each labelled with where it came from and how much to trust it. Built for Challenge 7 (Field Shift), it answers one question in seconds: what can I grow here, and is it safe to plant now?

It unifies NASA GIBS satellite imagery, NASA POWER climate records, NASA EONET natural events, NASA FIRMS fire detections, USGS earthquakes, Open-Meteo forecasts, ISRIC SoilGrids and GBIF biodiversity into a single 16-module workspace. Crop Atlas screens 617 species against ten years of climate and real mandi prices; God's Eye adds live aircraft, orbital tracking and hazard mapping; Event Radar, Rain Radar, Time Compare and a 3D expedition lab complete the picture.

Nothing is invented. Every value carries a measured, modelled or AI badge, and missing data is shown as missing.
details:
🌍 EARTHSCOPE GodView

A Global Earth Intelligence Workspace | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

Challenge 7 — Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data

Turning Earth observation into local understanding, practical decisions, and actionable evidence.

🌎 PROJECT OVERVIEW

EARTHSCOPE GodView is an interactive Earth intelligence workspace that transforms any location on the planet into a live, source-tagged evidence board.

Built for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Challenge 7: Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data, EARTHSCOPE helps farmers, students, researchers, and communities answer three important questions:

1. What is actually happening at this location?
2. What can realistically grow here?
3. What information can help guide the next decision?

Instead of forcing users to navigate disconnected scientific platforms, datasets, and tools, EARTHSCOPE brings relevant Earth-observation intelligence together in one accessible workspace.

🚀 WHAT DOES EARTHSCOPE DO?

EARTHSCOPE consolidates fragmented Earth-observation and environmental datasets into a unified, interactive experience.

Users can simply drop a pin anywhere on the 3D globe and explore a location-specific intelligence board containing:

  • 🌦️ Live Weather: Current and forecast weather conditions.
  • 🌡️ Climate History: Ten years of temperature and precipitation history.
  • 🌱 Soil Intelligence: Soil properties and chemical information.
  • 🌪️ Active Hazards: Natural events, disasters, and environmental alerts.
  • 🛰️ Satellite Imagery: Earth imagery and observation layers.
  • 🌾 Crop Suitability: Crop options screened against local climate and soil conditions.
  • 💹 Market Intelligence: Regional wholesale and mandi price information.
  • 📰 Regional News: Recent, location-relevant news and events.

Every insight is accompanied by its source and an indication of its confidence or information type.

🌾 The Crop Atlas — From Earth Data to Agricultural Decisions

At the heart of EARTHSCOPE is the Crop Atlas, which screens 617 crop species using real climate and soil information.

It compares ten years of temperature and precipitation data against published FAO EcoCrop climate envelopes, then incorporates soil texture and water-access inputs to produce a transparent 0–100 crop screening index.

The result connects two sides of agricultural decision-making:

Agronomic suitability: What crops may be suitable for the local environmental conditions?

Economic context: What are the reported regional wholesale market prices?

By bringing these insights together, EARTHSCOPE helps users evaluate both the environmental and economic dimensions of crop selection before planting.

Beyond the Crop Atlas, the platform brings together 16 connected modules spanning environmental hazards, radar, satellite imagery, biodiversity, recipes, 3D exploration, and AI assistance.

⚙️ HOW IT WORKS

EARTHSCOPE uses a unified data pipeline to transform information from public Earth-observation services and partner providers into accessible, location-specific insights.

The Data-to-Insight Pipeline

NASA and Partner Data Sources
↓
Server-Side Data Retrieval, Normalisation & Caching
↓
Unified API and Data Processing Layer
↓
Interactive Globe, Maps & Analytics
↓
Source-Tagged, Location-Specific Insights

Public data feeds are retrieved server-side, transformed into a consistent format, cached, and delivered to the browser through a unified API layer.

🌱 Transparent Crop Suitability Screening

The Crop Atlas evaluates agricultural suitability by comparing local climate conditions with published FAO EcoCrop requirements.

The screening process combines:

  • Ten years of gridded temperature data.
  • Ten years of gridded precipitation data.
  • Published FAO EcoCrop climate envelopes.
  • Soil texture information.
  • Water-access inputs.

These factors contribute to a transparent 0–100 screening index.

Importantly, this score is a screening tool — not a guarantee of harvest, yield, or agricultural success. It helps users identify potentially suitable crops while making the underlying factors visible.

🔍 Evidence, Not False Certainty

One of EARTHSCOPE's defining principles is that users should always understand the nature of the information they are viewing.

Every data point is visibly classified as:

  • MEASURED — Information reported by an observational or data provider.
  • MODELLED — Information derived from models, calculations, or processed datasets.
  • AI-INTERPRETED — Insights or responses generated with artificial intelligence.

Missing information is marked "Unavailable", never silently represented as zero. Coverage limitations are communicated, and market prices are identified as wholesale reports rather than guaranteed farm-gate offers.

💚 BENEFITS & REAL-WORLD IMPACT

EARTHSCOPE is designed to make complex Earth data useful to the people who need it.

🌾 For Farmers

  • Explore crop options based on local climate and soil conditions.
  • Review reported wholesale market prices before planting.
  • Use fertiliser and water-budget worksheets for planning.
  • Generate printable A4 field reports to carry into the field.
  • Access multiple sources of agricultural and environmental information in one place.

Potential impact: Better-informed agricultural planning through accessible environmental and economic evidence.

🛰️ For Researchers

  • Explore earthquakes, wildfires, floods, storms, and volcanic activity.
  • Access radar, satellite imagery, air-quality information, and soil properties.
  • Investigate biodiversity records and related environmental datasets.
  • Work with timestamped, source-linked information in a unified workspace.

Potential impact: Less time switching between fragmented platforms and more time investigating meaningful patterns.

🏘️ For Communities

  • Access multi-hazard situational awareness.
  • Explore environmental conditions and disaster-related information.
  • Understand data coverage limitations rather than relying on misleading completeness.
  • Use the platform in six languages, including Nepali, Hindi, Bengali, Maithili, English, and Spanish.

Potential impact: More accessible environmental information for communities across different regions and language backgrounds.

🎓 For Students & Educators

  • Explore real NASA Earth-observation data directly in a web browser.
  • Interact with an accessible 3D globe and mapping environment.
  • Learn how climate, soil, hazards, and biodiversity data connect.
  • Get started without installing specialist desktop software.

Potential impact: Bringing practical Earth-data exploration closer to classrooms, students, and independent learners.

🧠 TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES USED

EARTHSCOPE combines web technologies, geospatial visualisation, public scientific datasets, and AI-assisted capabilities.

💻 Backend

  • PHP 8
  • SQLite with MySQL support
  • RESTful API architecture
  • Server-side caching
  • API rate limiting

🎨 Frontend

  • Vanilla JavaScript (ES6)
  • MapLibre GL JS
  • Three.js
  • JSZip

🗺️ Mapping & Visualisation

  • MapLibre GL 3D Globe
  • NASA GIBS imagery tiles
  • OpenStreetMap
  • Esri World Imagery
  • AWS Terrain Tiles

🌐 Data Providers & Integrations

  • NASA GIBS
  • NASA POWER
  • NASA EONET
  • NASA CMR / NISAR
  • NASA FIRMS
  • USGS
  • Open-Meteo
  • ISRIC SoilGrids
  • GBIF
  • OpenStreetMap / Nominatim
  • RainViewer
  • GDACS
  • GDELT
  • ADSB.lol
  • Wikimedia Commons

  • API Ninjas
  • TheMealDB

📱 Platform & Accessibility

  • Progressive Web App (PWA)
  • Offline-capable application shell
  • Responsive interface designed for desktop and mobile
  • Light, dark, and night themes
  • Six-language AI assistant support

✨ CREATIVITY & DESIGN APPROACH

Our Core Design Philosophy: Don't Just Show Data. Explain What It Means.

The defining design decision behind EARTHSCOPE is refusing to fake certainty.

Many platforms display individual data layers. EARTHSCOPE aims to connect those layers to practical questions and decisions — while clearly communicating how reliable each insight is and where its limitations lie.

For example:

  • A crop suitability score is presented as a screening index, not a promise of a successful harvest.
  • A reported market price is labelled as a wholesale price, not a guaranteed price a farmer will receive.
  • Missing data is displayed as unavailable, not as zero.
  • Hazard information includes honest coverage limitations.
  • AI-generated interpretations are clearly separated from measured and modelled information.

🛰️ A Rich, Interactive Earth Exploration Environment

Around this evidence-first foundation, EARTHSCOPE offers a deliberately immersive interface inspired by tactical intelligence and scientific exploration systems.

Its connected capabilities include:

  • Tactical OSINT Command Centre: A unified environment for exploring location-specific intelligence.
  • Advanced Visualisation Modes: Night-vision, thermal, and synthetic-aperture-radar-inspired visual shaders.
  • Live Aircraft Tracking: Explore aircraft positions through integrated tracking data.
  • Orbital Satellite Tracking: View satellite ground tracks and orbital information.
  • 3D Expedition Lab: Explore satellite imagery and terrain through interactive driving, flying, and sailing experiences.
  • Browser-Based Object Detection: Analyse user-selected images without uploading them to a server.
  • Multilingual AI Assistant: Ask questions and explore Earth-related information in six languages.

16 connected modules. One unified workspace. No specialist installation required.

The aim is not simply to make Earth data look impressive. It is to make complex environmental information more understandable, explorable, and useful.

🌍 TEAM CONSIDERATIONS & RESPONSIBLE DESIGN

We prioritised four principles throughout the development of EARTHSCOPE:

1. Open-Data Ethics
The platform brings together publicly available datasets and aims to preserve source attribution and data provenance.

2. AI Transparency
AI-generated content is explicitly identified as AI interpretation and kept separate from measured and modelled data.

3. Honest Uncertainty Reporting
Missing information, dataset limitations, and screening-score limitations are communicated rather than hidden.

4. Global Accessibility
The workspace is designed to make Earth intelligence more accessible across regions, devices, and language backgrounds.

Our vision is simple:

A farmer in Nepal, a teacher in Kenya, and a researcher in Brazil should all be able to explore relevant Earth evidence in their own language — with the same transparent distinction between what is measured, what is modelled, and what is interpreted.
